subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved with latency-aware Slack docs/setup guidance for HTTP Request URLs, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists, but changing setup language or defaults affects Slack operator expectations, public ingress requirements, and upgrade guidance.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local and private deployments, and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode with explicit upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after maintainers decide no latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local and private deployments, and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the measurement, landed the partial current-main repair, and scoped the remaining HTTP guidance work.
